chapter: Pictures, Oliver, Armstrong and Fat Pichon
title: Closing questions: King Oliver and Louis Armstrong as a boy
summary: Arthur says King Oliver worked with his father and brother, and recalls Armstrong in the yards uptown as a boy.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Any other impressions, Russell? No. I should have mentioned on this tape in the beginning that Russell Levy is here also helping with the interviewer, this is Bill Russell, so we identify our voices on the tape in case the secretary later will be listening to this, to some of it to write down some of it. Is there anything else you'd like to add about either your life or the old times of dancing, anything else you can remember about your father or any of the other old time musicians? You did mention, I believe before we started, he played with Joe Oliver too, I think you said he worked with King Oliver.

Yeah, he worked with King Oliver. King Oliver worked with my daddy and worked with my brother. I remember King Oliver well, he was a big, heavy set dog fella, had a cataract on one eye. I remember him well, he was by my house right now, I remember him. I remember King Oliver well. And I remember Lewis Armstrong when he used to play in the yards uptown when he first started out. Now they had a picture of him when he was a boy in short pants in, what's this fella? Red, oh I can't remember, they had a place up here on Howard Street I think it was, right across from where the nightclub they got uptown there. Doudrop. Doudrop, yeah. Right across from the Doudrop they had a fella by the name of Red Batiste. And in this place, Red Batiste died, in this place they had a big frame and they had all those old time musicians in there. And even Lewis Armstrong when he was a boy in short pants.
